text:
Asha Patel: Quick heads-up — we're seeing partial failures in the reranking API during large batch ingestion jobs for a subset of accounts. Initial triage points to a regression in the KV cache eviction change from last week's runtime patch. Preparing customer-facing comms; need input on tone for renewal-risk accounts.

Miguel Alvarez: Which customers are impacted? any in renewal window this quarter?

Asha Patel: Impacted list is small: ~15 accounts, 4 are flagged as high-touch (renewal in next 60 days). Mitigation plan: roll back the eviction change to fallback behavior which should restore stable throughput. Target rollback ETA ~90 minutes.

Elliot Chen: We should include explicit SLA credit language for those high-touch accounts. Also propose a one-hour priority office hours slot tomorrow for full walkthroughs.

Ravi Singh: Copying legal for credit wording. From CS ops side: recommended comms are (1) a short proactive notice to all affected tenants, (2) a tailored outreach for the 4 renewal-risk customers with offer for live bridge and credit.

Jules Martin (Legal): We can sign off on a standard credit line — please avoid specific dollar amounts in the first message. Use: "We will evaluate eligibility for service credits under your agreement; our CS team will follow up to confirm any credits."

Asha Patel: Draft short customer email below (keeping it concise for production teams). Feedback welcome.

```
Subject: Brief outage note — reranking latency/failures for some batch jobs

Hi [Customer name],

We wanted to let you know we've detected intermittent failures impacting reranking calls for large batch ingestion jobs in your account. Our engineers have identified a regression in a recent runtime cache change and are rolling back the change now. We expect normal service to resume within ~90 minutes.

What we're doing:
- Rolling back the KV cache eviction change to restore stability.
- Monitoring your ingest jobs and prioritizing any backfill requests.
- Offering priority support and review for customers with upcoming renewals.

Next steps: our CS lead will reach out with a short update once service is restored and to discuss any credits or remediation. In the meantime, you can follow the incident at <status.redwood.ai/inc/INC-2026-542>.

We're sorry for the disruption and appreciate your patience.

— Asha, Customer Success
```

Miguel Alvarez: LGTM. For the high-touch renewal accounts, add a sentence: "We're available for a dedicated call to review impact and next steps — please let us know a preferred time this week."

Asha Patel: Will add. Also adding an internal AE/CS one-pager with impacted list and suggested credit language for quick approvals.

incident-bot: Incident created INC-2026-542 (priority: high). Postmortem meeting scheduled: tomorrow 10:00 AM PT.

Ravi Singh: Once Jules confirms wording we can send the general note to all affected and start 1:1 outreach for the renewal-risk cohort. Miguel — can your team own the tailored outreach?

Miguel Alvarez: Yep — I'll own the 1:1s and phối together with CS ops.

Asha Patel: Thank you — sending after legal ack. :thumbsup:
